then.text: Your boots are clean. Your pockets are clean. Your conscience, I've no jurisdiction. Move along.
Boots. Hands. Pockets. Let me see inside the lining of that rucksack. You've got a seed in your cuff. A SEED. Do you know what one seed does to this island?
Fine. You're clean. Have a good day, and mind the fur seals.

else.text: Every visitor, every boot. We've got the rats off this island and we'd like to keep them off. Come back with a reason, and you'll go through the boot wash.

then.text: The Boss! To the Boss! Hear, hear. I'd say more, but the wind has been saying it for a hundred years.
That's done. We'll never know what he'd have said. Probably 'Whose idea was this, and where's my breakfast?'
You've got the tot. Good. We stand at the foot, raise the glass, say 'The Boss', and pour a measure on the ground. It's wasteful and nobody minds.
You raise the tot. 'The Boss,' you say. The wind drops, for exactly one second, then thinks better of it.

else.text: Whisky, for the Boss. That's the tradition. I come here every year. This is the first year I've had the self-control to pour it out.

sg_wanderer.text: Eleven days from Ushuaia and I've seen four hundred thousand penguins. Do you know what the cabin steward asked? 'Have you got any boots?' Seven times.
I've decided I like fur seals best. They look cross about everything and it's refreshing. Don't tell the kings.

sg_departure.text: Brize Norton? There's a long haul, a lot of sea and a very rude albatross. I can arrange the lot.
